UPSTREAM: cpufreq: intel_pstate: Make HWP limits compatible with legacy To enable HWP on supported platforms. Reverted by 'commit a98b10da5fc5 ("Revert "UPSTREAM: cpufreq: intel_pstate: Make HWP limits compatible with legacy"") due to regression in graphics_SanAngeles > 20% on Baytrail. Patches related to HWP not responsible for regression. Regression due to 'commit 22f1cf724a5f ("UPSTREAM: cpufreq: intel_pstate: Account for non C0 time")' Under HWP the performance limits are calculated using max_perf_pct and min_perf_pct using possible performance, not available performance. The available performance can be reduced by no_turbo setting. To make compatible with legacy mode, use max/min performance percentage with respect to available performance. Signed-off-by: Srinivas Pandruvada <srinivas.pandruvada@linux.intel.com> Signed-off-by: Rafael J. Wysocki <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com> (cherry picked from commit 4e5d3f713b619e404618fc280ce861e473605f85) Signed-off-by: Aditya Swarup <aditya.swarup@intel.com> BUG=chrome-os-partner:61059 TEST=cd /sys/devices/system/cpu -> sysfs entry for intel_pstate/ iotools rdmsr 0(cpu no) 0x770 -> 1 (Intel HWP enabled) Run graphics_SanAngeles, performance doesn't regress by 20% Change-Id: Ie09a68d8a91cfeaaa5507a292d65a1cc2b427050 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/487007 Commit-Ready: Duncan Laurie <dlaurie@google.com> Tested-by: Michael Cheng <michael.cheng@intel.com> Reviewed-by: Chintan M Patel <chintan.m.patel@intel.com> Reviewed-by: Duncan Laurie <dlaurie@google.com> Reviewed-by: Puthikorn Voravootivat <puthik@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: cpufreq: intel_pstate: Calculate guaranteed performance for HWP To enable HWP on supported platforms. Reverted by 'commit a2f7ced835c5 ("Revert "UPSTREAM: cpufreq: intel_pstate: Calculate guaranteed performance for HWP"")' due to regression in graphics_SanAngeles > 20% on Baytrail. Patches related to HWP not responsible for regression. Regression due to 'commit 22f1cf724a5f ("UPSTREAM: cpufreq: intel_pstate: Account for non C0 time")' When HWP is active, turbo activation ratio is not used to calculate max non turbo ratio. But on these systems the max non turbo ratio is decided by config TDP settings. This change removes usage of MSR_TURBO_ACTIVATION_RATIO for HWP systems, instead directly use TDP ratios, when more than one TDPs are available. Signed-off-by: Srinivas Pandruvada <srinivas.pandruvada@linux.intel.com> Signed-off-by: Rafael J. Wysocki <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com> (cherry picked from commit 8fc7554ae5cc381e18bffa2469333ad28453d557) Signed-off-by: Aditya Swarup <aditya.swarup@intel.com> BUG=chrome-os-partner:61059 TEST=cd /sys/devices/system/cpu -> sysfs entry for intel_pstate/ iotools rdmsr 0(cpu no) 0x770 -> 1 (Intel HWP enabled) Run graphics_SanAngeles, performance doesn't regress by 20% Change-Id: I88629cf167506be16e5872b2ff561e574d218721 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/487008 Commit-Ready: Duncan Laurie <dlaurie@google.com> Tested-by: Michael Cheng <michael.cheng@intel.com> Reviewed-by: Chintan M Patel <chintan.m.patel@intel.com> Reviewed-by: Duncan Laurie <dlaurie@google.com> Reviewed-by: Puthikorn Voravootivat <puthik@chromium.org>

BACKPORT: cpufreq: intel_pstate: Correct frequency setting in the HWP mode To enable HWP on supported platforms. Reverted by 'commit b30f61089eaf ("Revert "BACKPORT: cpufreq: intel_pstate: Correct frequency setting in the HWP mode"")' due to regression in graphics_SanAngeles > 20% on Baytrail. Patches related to HWP not responsible for regression. Regression due to 'commit 22f1cf724a5f ("UPSTREAM: cpufreq: intel_pstate: Account for non C0 time")' In the functions intel_pstate_hwp_set(), min/max range from HWP capability MSR along with max_perf_pct and min_perf_pct, is used to set the HWP request MSR. In some cases this doesn't result in the correct HWP max/min in HWP request. For example: In the following case: HWP capabilities from MSR 0x771 0x70a1220 Here cpufreq min/max frequencies from above MSR dump are 700MHz and 3.2GHz respectively. This will result in hwp_min = 0x07 hwp_max = 0x20 To limit max frequency to 2GHz: perf_limits->max_perf_pct = 63 (2GHz as a percent of 3.2GHz rounded up) With the current calculation: adj_range = max_perf_pct * range / 100; adj_range = 63 * (32 - 7) / 100 adj_range = 15 max = hw_min + adj_range; max = 7 + 15 = 22 This will result in HWP request of 0x160f, which will result in a frequency cap of 2.2GHz not 2GHz. The problem with the above calculation is that hwp_min of 7 is treated as 0% in the range. But max_perf_pct is calculated with respect to minimum as 0 and max as 3.2GHz or hwp_max, so adding hwp_min to it will result in more than the desired. Since the min_perf_pct and max_perf_pct is already a percent of max frequency or hwp_max, this min/max HWP request value can be calculated directly applying these percentage to hwp_max. Signed-off-by: Srinivas Pandruvada <srinivas.pandruvada@linux.intel.com> Signed-off-by: Rafael J. Wysocki <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com> (cherry picked from commit 3f8ed54aee491bbb83656592c2d0ad7b78d045ca) Signed-off-by: Aditya Swarup <aditya.swarup@intel.com> Conflicts: drivers/cpufreq/intel_pstate.c Remove unused variables To avoid conflict in intel_pstate_hwp_set due to upstream linux 'commit eae48f046ffa ("cpufreq: intel_pstate: Per CPU P-State limits")' assign global perf limits variable to perf_limits Set min and max perf limit for hwp using perf_limits BUG=chrome-os-partner:61059 TEST=cd /sys/devices/system/cpu -> sysfs entry for intel_pstate/ iotools rdmsr 0(cpu no) 0x770 -> 1 (Intel HWP enabled) Run graphics_SanAngeles, performance doesn't regress by 20% Change-Id: I3e002e4d050de8c2902e2e5f7d08203e7b9ffadd Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/487009 Commit-Ready: Duncan Laurie <dlaurie@google.com> Tested-by: Michael Cheng <michael.cheng@intel.corp-partner.google.com> Reviewed-by: Chintan M Patel <chintan.m.patel@intel.com> Reviewed-by: Duncan Laurie <dlaurie@google.com> Reviewed-by: Puthikorn Voravootivat <puthik@chromium.org>

io_jail: Add a wrapper around minijail The io_jail is used to jail io processes run from crosvm. Under the hood it mostly configures a minijail jail to run in. The minijail restrictions are applied when iojail::enter is called. This closes extra FDs and calls minijail_enter. The minijail_run* functions are left out as we don't have a need to exec foreign programs. libminijail will be used to jail separate processes spawned from the main crosvm process. The ability to close all open file descriptors is added. Minijail only closes FDs after forking and before exec. Change-Id: Ida7f52022c934e9e6edeb7b604cd6e6399860cb9 Signed-off-by: Dylan Reid <dgreid@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/505100 Reviewed-by: Zach Reizner <zachr@chromium.org>

Clean up GenericRetry. Introduced |status_callback| to the GenericRetry. Then; - Migrate success_functor to the callback. The only caller was cidb, and modified the callback. - Migrate metrics counter update. The callers were only patch and repository, so updated them, too. Note that the timing to update the counter is changed from "before" attempt to "after" attempt. Specifically, in this design because the callback is called after the attempt in which anything can happen, it may not be called always. Practical drawback is, in general, maybe loosing some logging info. Considering current use case, it is not the big deal, at the moment. This is preparation to refactor it to the decorator style.
